svg.title: Power Platform MCP servers, their clients and the controls between them
svg.desc: Left, the clients: a Copilot Studio agent (built-in MCP connectors, the onboarding wizard or a custom connector), a Foundry agent (MCP tool with server label, allowed tools, approval setting and a project connection), a Microsoft 365 Copilot declarative agent (MCP plugin that can render MCP Apps widgets) and developer tools (VS Code with GitHub Copilot, GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude). Right, the Power Platform MCP servers: the Dataverse MCP server at /api/mcp with generally available tools for search, describe, read_query, record and table changes, skills and files, plus /api/mcp_preview for preview tools; the Power Apps MCP server, preview, with log_for_review, request_assistance and invoke_data_entry for the agent feed; the App MCP of a model-driven app, preview, which generates a declarative agent with grid and form tools and custom tools with HTML widgets; the Power Pages MCP server, preview, governed by web roles and table permissions; the PAC CLI MCP server, local over stdio, for developers; a published Copilot Studio agent exposed as an MCP server through the MCP client channel, early release; and Dynamics 365 MCP servers available as connectors. Bottom right, your own server, such as Cedar Dispatch C-56. In the middle, the controls: the Power Platform admin center turns the Dataverse MCP server on per environment and lists the allowed clients (Copilot Studio on by default; GitHub Copilot, the Dataverse CLI and custom Microsoft Entra apps by client ID); data policies govern MCP servers used through connectors in Copilot Studio; Dataverse security roles apply to the identity that calls; Dataverse MCP tools are charged in Copilot Credits when the agent is built outside Copilot Studio.

1. Whose identity reaches the data? The signed-in user (OAuth passthrough, delegated), the agent (agent identity,
app role) or a shared key. Dataverse decides with that identity's security roles.
2. Which tools may the agent see? Turn tools off in Copilot Studio, or list allowed_tools in Foundry.
3. Who confirms a write? require_approval in Foundry, a confirmation step or no write tool at all in Copilot Studio.
